title: Coherent enriched graphs and their ordered-pair evaluation
statement: Use the monoidal infinity category $p:\mathcal V^\otimes\to\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$, the universe conventions, and the universal point family $q:U\to\mathcal S$ of small spaces underlying the total algebroid construction of [def-coef-complete-algebroid]. A $\mathcal V$-enriched graph is a small space $X$ and a coherent functor $X\times X\to\mathcal V$, with no compositions or units. Define $\operatorname{Graph}(\mathcal V)$ as the total infinity category with these fibers and restriction along maps of spaces; a morphism over $f:X\to Y$ is a coherent transformation $G\to(f\times f)^*H$. Its simplices are coherent functors on the square of the universal point family pulled back to a parameter simplex. Values are in the actual fiber $\mathcal V$ over $[1]$. The object-space projection remembers $X$. The canonical forgetful functor $\operatorname{Algd}(\mathcal V)\to\operatorname{Graph}(\mathcal V)$ restricts the algebroid functor to ordered pairs over $[1]$. The ordered-pair category has objects $(G,x,y)$, retains coherent transport of both marked objects, and has the evaluation functor $(G,x,y)\mapsto G(x,y)$ to $\mathcal V$.
